blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Recovery Demonstration Curation**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Trajectory Curation, § Recovery Demonstration Curation
blocks.md: When an agent issues a malformed tool call, receives a rejection from the environment runtime, and then inspects the schema to produce a passing patch, its trace records both a mistake and a valid repair. A naive curation pipeline might discard this trace because it contains a failed step, or edit out the error to make the agent appear infallible. Either choice discards the evidence of how to recover from an imperfect prefix.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Recovery demonstrations matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A policy trained only on clean prefixes meets off-path states it never saw, so recovery demonstrations keep the mistake as conditioning context and select only the assessed correction as the target.

questions.q: The section **Recovery Demonstration Curation** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A failure earns a weight update only if it persists with complete context, a well-formed interface, and a healthy runtime, so counterfactual probes run up the intervention ladder from context and schema to SFT and then RL.
Every record version carries a lineage envelope, and any transformation creates a derived record that inherits its source's split group and use permission, so withdrawal reaches every descendant.

Admission is a route-specific conjunction of predicate families that each resolve to pass, fail, pending, or unknown, a missing check never defaults to pass, and checks are ordered by cost per rejection.
A policy trained only on clean prefixes meets off-path states it never saw, so recovery demonstrations keep the mistake as conditioning context and select only the assessed correction as the target.
